definition: The practice does not reduce the yield loss caused by the hazard.
The practice prevents a small part of the loss: up to about a quarter.
The practice prevents around half of the loss.
The practice prevents most of the loss: about three quarters.
The practice prevents the loss entirely: yield under the hazard is the same as in a normal season.

Drought: season rainfall below the crop's requirement, taken as the lower end of the Concern Worldwide range (maize: under 500 mm). Heat: daily maximum temperature in the crop's heat window above its moderate threshold, the lowest optimum upper end among the window's stages (maize 30 C). Thresholds and windows are cc4a-hazards decisions 0006 and 0007; how many days make a season count is that pipeline's open point.
Drought: season rainfall below 80 % of the requirement (maize: under 400 mm). Heat: daily maximum in the heat window above the midpoint between the moderate and extreme thresholds (maize 33 C).

Drought: season rainfall below 60 % of the requirement (maize: under 300 mm, the least Concern says short-season maize withstands). Heat: daily maximum in the heat window above the lowest ceiling among the window's stages (maize 36 C).
Rests on single studies, on evidence from outside Africa only, on expert judgement, or on reasoning from the mechanism.
A meta-analysis or synthesis exists but with few African studies, or the sources disagree on the size of the effect while agreeing on its direction.
At least one meta-analysis or synthesis with substantial African data, and the sources agree on direction and rough size.
The practice can be used with this commodity group.
Only under a condition stated in the note (for example, only where a cover crop fits in the season).
The practice is not relevant to this commodity group. Nothing is computed for the pair.
Too little rainfall for the crop over its growing season: the season total against the crop's requirement, over the season window of cc4a-hazards (decision 0004).
Days too hot for the crop in its heat window: flowering to the end of seed filling for seed crops, the whole season for roots and tubers (cc4a-hazards decision 0007).
A published quantitative meta-analysis. First choice.
A systematic or narrative review, or a synthesis database such as ERA or Rural Scan.
A single trial or survey. Used where no meta-analysis or synthesis covers the case.
Our own compilation or analysis, done where published evidence is lacking.
A judgement by a named expert, with the reasoning written in the finding.
The finding supports a row of the yield benefit table.
The finding supports a row of the hazard mitigation table.
The finding supports a row of the hazard loss table.
The finding describes where or under what conditions a practice's effect holds (supports the applicability table).
The source averages over all seasons, good and bad together. Usual for meta-analyses.
The source reports seasons without climate stress.
The source reports seasons under the hazard.
The source reports the effect separately for normal and stressed seasons or conditions, as a contrast within one finding.
The source does not say.
Evidence from sub-Saharan Africa.
Evidence from Africa including North Africa.
Global evidence, or evidence from outside Africa.
Use the Concern Worldwide value.
Use the EcoCrop value because Concern gives none that is usable.
The finding was read from the full text, with a page, table or figure locator.
The finding was read from the abstract only. Re-read against the full text before use in a table.
The finding comes from another source's summary (for example a review or ERA record), not the original.
Drought: loss = ky x (1 - season supply / requirement), between 0 and 100 % (Doorenbos and Kassam 1979).
Heat: loss = 1 - exp(-k x degree days above the crop's moderate threshold over its heat window), the log-yield form of Lobell et al. 2011.
No loss from this hazard for this crop (evidence of no effect).
Not computed yet: a perennial whose losses lag and carry over between years; needs a multi-season metric.
Parameters from evidence for this crop.
Parameters borrowed from another crop (proxy_commodity), for the reason in the note.
The general rule, derived for maize and applied to this crop.
No parameters yet.
Proposed; not yet reviewed.
Accepted for use.
